answer.main_body: cycad palm trunk and frond crown
answer.evidence: The cycad is drawn in pure side-scroller front elevation: the trunk base ends in perfectly flat horizontal pixel lines at rows 44-46 without any ground footprint curve, and the frond rosette is arranged vertically (upright back fronds, forward-facing central cone, and downward-hanging front fronds) with no top-down foreshortening or visible top surfaces.

The cycad crown is viewed from an elevated angle, showing fronds radiating in full depth: rear fronds rise from rows 12-18 behind the central cone/core, while foreground fronds droop down to row 34, giving ~13 rows of foreshortened top surface before reaching the south-facing overhang.

The cycad canopy is rendered in 3/4 perspective with clear depth layering: rear fronds rise higher (rows 12-16), a central cone/growing center is angled toward the viewer (rows 14-25), and foreground fronds hang down overlapping the upper trunk (rows 26-34).

answer.main_body: cycad trunk and crown of fronds
answer.evidence: The cycad is drawn in flat front elevation: fronds fan out entirely in the 2D vertical plane with no south-facing foreshortened fronds or view into the top of the crown from above. The central cone and shoot are seen straight-on, and the trunk base terminates in a completely flat horizontal line.
